content:
alex: Quick question — are we changing the embeddings endpoint contract for vectors when input is an array of mixed types? I skimmed the PR. Specifically: truncation rules for long texts, handling non-string inputs (bytes/arrays), batch size limits and how we report vector length when using quantized models. Need this for docs + client SDKs. Pinged in PR but wanted async answer here.

maria-w: We shouldn't change the contract for existing models. PR proposes returning same shape [n_inputs, dim]. Backwards compatible unless model dim changes.

samir: Correct. Implementation notes: if input is non-string (e.g., list of tokens) we normalize to string via json.dumps on server side, then run tokenizer. Truncation: we truncate to token_limit (config per model) and attach 'truncated': true in the response meta for each input.

jin: Also note batch limits: max_batch_size=2048 tokens across batch; if exceeded we split and return multiple invocations internally. From API perspective we always return vectors for all inputs in order.

eva-ml: Example payload I used in tests:
```json
{
  "inputs": ["short", "" , [1,2,3], {"text":"hello"}],
  "model": "redwood-embed-v1"
}
```

Response shape:

```json
{
  "data": [
    {"id": 0, "embedding": [0.0012, 0.0234, 0.0001, ...], "meta": {"truncated": false}},
    {"id": 1, "embedding": [...], "meta": {"truncated": true}},
    {"id": 2, "embedding": [...], "meta": {"normalized_from": "list"}},
    {"id": 3, "embedding": [...], "meta": {"normalized_from": "object"}}
  ],
  "model_dim": "1536"
}
```

samir: vector length is always model_dim (string in meta historically, but we should keep numeric-aware docs). For quantized models we still decompress to float32 in response; we don't return quant tensors.

maria-w: Docs action: alex can you update client SDK note about normalize behavior and include 'truncated' flag? Also mention we preserve input order even if we split batches.

alex: Yes, I'll update the JS + Python clients. Quick clarification: when we split internal batches do we surface any header like X-Partial-Batches or are logs only? I want deterministic retries in clients.

jin: No header. We don't expose internal splits. If we fail part-way we return 500 with partial_error field containing index ranges. Otherwise success is full set.

eva-ml: QA note: add unit tests around non-string inputs — we had a bug where bytes caused tokenizer to error.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled for 2024-02-14 02:00 UTC; any regressions must be flagged before 2024-02-12 EOD.

alex: Thanks. I'll add SDK changes + unit tests and tag @samir for code review when ready.

samir: Sounds good. LMK when PR is up. :thumbsup:
